messages:
alex kim: Noticed ~35% token/sec drop on prod after last release (merged PR #1024). Canary latency spikes and general throughput down. Anyone else see this?

mira patel: Yep saw alerts from SLOs at 06:12. Token/sec from our smoke tests dropped 1200 -> ~780. :grimacing:

ci-bot: CI perf check failed for commit 1759abc on branch release/v1.4. Metrics: tokens_per_sec -34%, p95_latency +22%. See: https://ci.internal/runs/7890

devon li: putting up quick profiler snapshot from the canary (top kernels):
```
kernel_select: l2_matmul_q8 -> selected_quantized_matmul
time(ms):  baseline  0.9  current 1.6
attention_cpu: baseline 0.6  current 0.7
KV_cache_lookup: baseline 0.3  current 0.9
Total token time: baseline 0.83ms -> current 1.25ms
```

sanjay rao: That kv_cache_lookup jump looks suspicious. PR #1019 changed scheduler heuristics to prefer larger batches and also adjusted the kernel selector thresholds for quantized mats. Might be interacting poorly with prefix caching.

alex kim: Stack traces / logs show queueing delays piling up. Example log from runtime:
```
[2026-01-09T06:11:54Z] queue: waiting 14ms, attempted batch_size=16, drained=0
[2026-01-09T06:11:54Z] scheduler: max_batch_wait_ms=12 -> scheduling batch 4 after timeout
[2026-01-09T06:11:54Z] kernel: picked quant_matmul_v2 for seq_len=1024
```

mira patel: If max_batch_wait_ms=12 and actual waits hit 14ms we're falling back to tiny batches frequently. That plus picking a slower quant kernel could explain token/sec drop.

devon li: Running quick git bisect locally now between commit 172a..1759abc to find the regression point. Will post results in ~10m.

devon li: bisect finishes: culprit is commit 1759abc (scheduler: increase prefer_large_batch threshold + kernel selector change). Reproducer: heavy small-request workload causes queue accumulation, more frequent small-timeout-triggered flushes.

alex kim: Nice. Can we revert the kernel selector change separately and keep the batching heuristics? Which part caused the KV cache lookup spike?

devon li: Looking at diffs — the selector now prefers quantized_matmul_v2 for shapes near power-of-two seq lengths; that kernel allocates a temporary buffer causing extra memory traffic and cache disruption which spikes KV lookup times. Combined with smaller effective batches we're seeing both higher per-token kernel time and increased queue churn.

mira patel: Mitigation options: 1) revert commit 1759abc (hotfix), 2) tweak max_batch_wait_ms down to 6ms to force earlier flushes (temporary), 3) pin kernel selection policy to previous selector in runtime config.

alex kim: Can someone open a revert PR for the kernel selector portion and a config change for canary? I'll mark this rollout-blocker.

devon li: PR #1035 opened: revert(kernel-selector changes from 1759abc) — running CI. Also pushed a canary config change to reduce max_batch_wait_ms in prod canary pools.

ci-bot: CI perf check queued for PR #1035.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for release/v1.4 due to perf regression. Rolling back canary pool overrides to previous config in 5m unless hotfix merges.

mira patel: After applying canary config change, smoke test token/sec recovered to ~1150 (vs 780). Still slightly under baseline but much better.

alex kim: Good. If CI for revert passes, we'll merge and promote. Also add a perf test that exercises kv cache hit churn to avoid regression going forward.

sanjay rao: I'll add an eval harness test that simulates many short requests with repeated prefixes. Will add to the nightly perf suite + alert if token/sec drops >10% vs baseline.

alex kim: Thanks all — keeping this thread pinned until resolved. :thumbsup:
